 DETROIT (United States), 02/11/2026.- Voters fill out their ballots to vote in the midterm election on the last day of early voting at the City of Detroit Department of Elections in Detroit, Michigan, USA, 02 November 2026. (Elecciones) EFE/EPA/SARAH YENESEL NEWSROOM CLARIN As voters across the United States head to polling places for the high-stakes 2026 midterm elections , many residents find themselves wondering how standard daily commerce and public services are affected. 
 Because election administration is decentralized and rules vary widely by jurisdiction, knowing what is open or closed can prevent scheduling headaches. Here is your definitive guide to business hours, mail delivery, financial markets, and state holiday rules for Election Day. 
 Is Election Day a Federal Holiday?
 No. Election Day is not one of the official 11 federal holidays designated by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management.
 Because it is not a federal closure day, federal government offices (outside of specific state-level observances), standard corporate businesses, financial institutions, and retail stores operate under completely normal business hours . The next official federal holiday is Veterans Day on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.
 What Is OPEN on Election Day?
 Since standard federal closures do not apply, the vast majority of commercial and delivery services are fully operational:
 Mail and Delivery Services: The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) is operating completely as normal, with post offices open and mail delivered. Private carriers—including FedEx, UPS, and Amazon fulfillment networks—are making standard deliveries.
 Banks and Financial Institutions: Major commercial banks (such as Bank of America, Chase, Citibank, and Wells Fargo) are open for regular branch transactions.
 Stock and Bond Markets: Wall Street is fully operational. Both the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the Nasdaq are running on their normal trading schedules, alongside bond markets.
 Retail and Grocery Stores: Major national chains, supermarkets, and local retail stores are open under regular hours.
 What Is CLOSED or Variable on Election Day?
 While national commerce continues as usual, certain public services and localized facilities face adjustments:
 Public Schools: Many local school districts are closed on Election Day—or operating on modified schedules—because a significant number of public schools serve as official neighborhood polling locations and security hubs.
 State and Local Government Offices: Rules depend entirely on your state. Several states (including Illinois, Maryland, New York, Hawaii, West Virginia, Delaware, Indiana, Kentucky, and Montana) classify Election Day as a state or public holiday, resulting in the closure of specific state government offices, such as the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).
 State Laws on Employer Voting Leave
 While Election Day is not a universal holiday , many states recognize the importance of ballot access by regulating employer requirements:
 Paid Voting Leave States: Numerous states (including New York, California, Illinois, Texas, and Colorado) legally require employers to provide workers with dedicated time off—frequently up to two or three hours of paid leave—so that employees whose work shifts overlap with polling hours can cast their ballots without penalty.
 Check your specific state secretary of state office website to confirm local employer compliance mandates and voting rights in your workplace.
